sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on orthographic 2.5D, with a vertically scrolling mine cutaway
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU on hardware adapters and WebGL 2 compatibility for software adapters; Rapier 3D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; optional PeerJS 1.5.5 / WebRTC
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural stylized cel shading, faceted mine rock, ink silhouettes, teal shadows and warm safety orange
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for breathing, walking, jet flight, rotors, rescue signals and creature motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only synthesized adaptive music (10% default), procedural sound effects and formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 player host-authoritative AI Hub shared-world co-op; standalone room codes using WebRTC / PeerJS and BroadcastChannel; two-player couch co-op. Hub and same-browser rooms verified; cross-internet connectivity unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium, complete default-balance physical-controls playthrough, keyboard/mouse, simulated DualSense, Xbox glyphs, multitouch, offline audio measurement, standalone two-page co-op and official 2/4-player AI Hub harness with impaired network, host departure and playerless host. State checks suspend drawing; visual checks use WebGL compatibility. Hardware WebGPU and physical controllers unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet search or source research. Native model knowledge; downloaded the explicitly supplied AI Hub integration specification/client/harness and required engine dependencies.

testingFeedback: 4 confirmed issues: charges fell past rubble, decorative menu arrows polluted accessible button names, the software WebGPU adapter lost or stalled, and formatting changed a build marker so credits metadata was not injected. All were addressed. Flawed test assumptions were tracked separately from product defects.

2 blockers: charge placement could prevent progression, and an unusable graphics backend could leave the scene blank. Charges now attach to nearby rubble; known software adapters use compatibility rendering, with device-loss recovery available.

The complete physical-controls campaign at default balance: all 3 miners, all 3 passages, all 12 creatures, 3 charges, no suit losses, no teleport, invulnerability or no-clip; approximately 81 seconds of simulated play.

Native software-WebGPU screenshots were least helpful: a blank or stalled capture did not establish gameplay correctness. A minimal cube isolated the driver problem; state assertions and compatibility screenshots were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL node materials made the cel-shaded palette consistent, and AnimationMixer reused native keyframe animation for characters, rotors and creatures.

Yes. The supplied software WebGPU path could lose or stall its device, including with a minimal cube. I used explicit compatibility selection for repeatable tests and automatic software-adapter selection in the game. Hardware WebGPU is unknown.
The rescue simulation, controller-first menu/input layer, and host-authoritative multiplayer protocol were the largest systems built around the renderer and Rapier.
Diagnosing headless graphics behavior while keeping a portable single HTML with embedded JavaScript and WebAssembly dependencies.
none; the engine libraries are unmodified. Adapter selection and device-loss recovery are application code.
I would add clear backend health reporting and automatic recovery when a device becomes unusable.
promptFeedback: The source inspiration, controller-first philosophy and concrete rescue-demo requirements gave the mechanics and presentation a clear focus.

The ban on internet research overlaps the required linked integration specification. I treated downloading that specification and dependencies as implementation work, without internet search or source-game research.
Combining a portable single-file 3D game, several input methods, authoritative co-op and meaningful headless verification while diagnosing the software graphics driver.

State explicitly whether WebGL compatibility is acceptable when a software WebGPU adapter is unusable, and distinguish required acceptance checks from optional physical-device or cross-internet verification.

aiHub.name: H.E.R.O. Another Day
aiHub.tagline: Three miners. One jetpack. Still your shift.
aiHub.description: Descend a living mine, blast blocked passages and tether three stranded miners back to the last lift. Dodge cave creatures, flooded workings and lava in a cel-shaded rescue adventure, solo or with a crew.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / A,D; fly: Cross / Space or W; aim: right stick / mouse; pulse: R2 / left click; charge: Square / E; rescue: Triangle / F; pause: Options / Esc. Touch: left thumb moves and flies, right thumb aims and fires.
